demand.reason: Global selenium consumption is estimated at roughly 3,600 metric tons annually, placing it squarely within the modest-demand band of 500–10,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is projected to experience low growth (1-5% CAGR). Steady, mature industrial and agricultural uses are expanding slowly, driving a balanced but slow upward trajectory.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: Selenium is recovered as a byproduct of copper anode slimes. Copper mine production is distributed across many countries, with the largest producer (Chile) at 23%. With no single country exceeding 30%, mining tracks at Score 1.


Refining: Refined selenium output tracks the copper metallurgical chain. China was the leading producer of refined selenium in 2025, accounting for 2,000 of about 3,800 tons (53%), placing refining concentration in the 50–65% band (Score 3). The world total excludes US output, which USGS withholds, so China's true share is probably close to 50%.

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Global reserves are tied to identified copper deposits. The estimated 92,000 tonnes of selenium contained in copper reserves equates to roughly 25 years of supply at current production rates, placing it in the 15–30 year band.


Diversification: Reserves track global copper ores, yielding an HHI of approximately 0.20, with Russia holding 28.3% and Peru 17.4%. This positions the geographic endowment in the well-distributed index band (0.15–0.25).

end_use.reason:
Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): selenium functions as a key material in CIGS thin-film solar cells. Construction & Heavy Industry (+0.5): utilized as a decolorizing agent in glass manufacturing and as a free-machining additive in steel alloys. Healthcare & Biomedical (+1.0): applied in pharmaceutical anti-dandruff shampoos and human dietary supplements. Agriculture & Food Security (+0.5): serves as a major input for livestock dietary supplements and selenium-enriched fertilizers.


Sector presence scores total 3.5 across 4 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus for 4 sectors adds +1.5, yielding an objective composite score of 5.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Silicon is a commercially deployed replacement in rectifiers; amorphous silicon and cadmium telluride compete in thin-film solar cells; and cerium oxide substitutes as a glass decolorant. Substitutes are proven and in use with moderate performance or cost trade-offs, matching Score 2.


Recyclability: Secondary recovery is active but restricted to manufacturing scrap and e-waste, yielding an estimated 5–8% of supply. The vast majority of consumption goes into highly dissipative uses (agriculture, glass, metallurgy) making end-of-life recovery economically marginal, placing it in the low but non-trivial 5–20% recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Selenium extraction requires specialized multi-stage hydrometallurgy. It is separated from electrolytic copper anode slimes via roasting, precipitation, and distillation. The process requires handling toxic intermediates and integration with large-scale base metal operations, characterizing it as complex and specialized.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is dependent on copper refining expansions. While global copper capacity is growing, recovery infrastructure is not expanding proportionally because installing selenium circuits is optional for copper smelters. Projects like the Bor refinery expansion in Serbia provide a thin pipeline with potential 5–10% supply additions.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India refined about 88 tons of selenium in 2024 and 90 tons in 2025 (USGS), recovered from copper anode slime at Hindalco and Kutch Copper (which has 150 tons a year of capacity), against consumption of several hundred tons. Production accounts for <20% of domestic consumption, placing India in the marginal domestic production band.


Strategic Posture: Selenium is notified on India's official 30 critical minerals list. However, there is no active KABIL mandate, no specific signed offtake agreements, and no targeted government-backed capacity expansions, aligning with passive awareness and no institutional action.

price_volatility.reason: Selenium prices experienced a 65% increase from trough to peak over the five-year window (moving from $14.58/kg to ~$24/kg), accompanied by notable intra-year quarterly spikes. The opaque, bilateral broker market drives moderate volatility within a 50–100% band.

capability.name: Selenium
capability.next_move: Fill Kutch Copper's 150 t/yr selenium capacity and add high-purity refining; India still imports more than it makes.
capability.what_india_has: About 90 t refined in 2025 from anode slime at Hindalco Dahej and Kutch Copper; 150 t/yr of capacity at Kutch Copper; Hindustan Copper's Ghatsila plant, which last reported selenium in 2006-07.
capability.cost: Small next to the smelter: Kutch Copper phase 1 cost about US$1.2 bn for 0.5 Mt/yr of copper (#7).

stages.world: A by-product of copper; copper mining is spread (Chile 23%).
China 2,000 of 3,800 t (2025); Japan 640 t; Russia 320 t.
stages.india: 88 t in 2024 and 90 t in 2025 (USGS). Hindalco refines selenium to over 99% at Dahej; Kutch Copper lists 150 t/yr.

stages.world: Glass, manganese electrolysis, alloys, feed additives, thin-film solar.
stages.india: India imports most of its selenium: 387 t in 2022-23, against exports of 184 t.

strategyList.name: Copper smelting and anode-slime treatment
strategyList.what: Smelting concentrate, electrorefining copper, then treating anode slime for gold, silver, selenium, tellurium and PGMs.
strategyList.outside_china: China 48% of refined copper; DRC, Chile, Japan. Tellurium from slime: Japan, Russia, Sweden, Canada, US (Rio Tinto).
strategyList.cost: Kutch Copper phase 1: ~US$1.2 bn for 0.5 Mt/yr. Tellurium circuit at Kennecott: US$2.9 m for ~20 t/yr.
strategyList.india_base: Hindalco (Dahej), Kutch Copper (0.5 Mt/yr), Vedanta (Silvassa); CSIR-IMMT's tellurium process listed at Hindalco.
strategyList.gap: Concentrate supply; commercial tellurium circuits and 5N refining.
